bull.t: Data‑center leadership and durable AI demand
bull.b: NVIDIA’s dominant data‑center traction—massive YoY growth and sequential gains—reflects durable structural demand for AI compute from hyperscalers and model makers. Large, recurring upgrade cycles and networking/system sales create a high‑margin, sticky revenue base over the next 2–6 months and beyond.

bull.t: Very strong cash generation and conservative balance sheet
bull.b: Exceptional FCF conversion (~0.95x of net income) and a very strong balance sheet (low leverage cited) give NVIDIA durable financial flexibility to fund R&D, capital commitments, buybacks and dividend policy. High cash conversion supports long‑term investment and shareholder return programs without immediate financing stress.

bull.t: Product leadership and ecosystem moat (Blackwell & software)
bull.b: Benchmark dominance and a deep software stack (CUDA/AI platform) create structural competitive advantages and high switching costs. Rapid architecture ramps and roadmap items (e.g., Vera CPU opening a large TAM) expand addressable markets and strengthen long‑term customer lock‑in across cloud, enterprise and HPC segments.

bear.t: Supply constraints and large prepaid commitments
bear.b: Heavy prepaid supply commitments and ongoing supply constraints raise execution risk: constrained shipments can delay revenue realization, force premium pricing or customer rationing, and inflate working capital. Over multiple quarters this can cap growth and create delivery‑related margin volatility.

bear.t: China export uncertainty and revenue exclusion
bear.b: Excluding China compute revenue from guidance highlights material geopolitical and regulatory risk. Losing or restricting access to a major addressable market increases concentration risk and reduces revenue visibility, complicating medium‑term planning and potentially curbing growth if restrictions persist.

Rapid OpEx expansion—driven by compensation and infrastructure—raises fixed costs and increases operating leverage. If revenue growth moderates, sustained higher OpEx could compress margins and reduce free cash flow generation relative to current peaks, making profitability more sensitive to demand cycles.
